facts.text: Warwick, New York, was named after an English town near the ancestral home of early settler Benjamin Aske in the early 1700s.
Officially established as a town in 1788, Warwick has been a Hudson Valley community for over two centuries.
The Warwick Valley Railroad, built in 1860, linked the village to the Lehigh and Hudson River Railway and spurred growth.
Historic preservation efforts by the Warwick Historical Society restored downtown buildings and earned the village listings on state and national historic registers.
The Albert Wisner Library, dedicated in 1927, remains a cornerstone of Warwick’s cultural life.
Warwick encompasses three villages—Florida, Greenwood Lake, and Warwick—and eight hamlets, including Amity, Bellvale, and Pine Island.
